headline: KSE-100 plunges 3,079 points to 168,865 as Brent tops $101 on Hormuz tanker war, Wall Street falls a fourth day on hot PPI
mood: Risk-off deepens · Hormuz tanker war and hawkish Fed repricing dominate

snapshot.label: Brent / WTI
snapshot.delta: highest since May · Hormuz tanker war

five_things.html: The benchmark shed 3,078.55 points (1.79%) to close at 168,865.04 on Thursday, its steepest single-day drop in weeks, as intensifying US-Iran strikes on tankers near the Strait of Hormuz and a surging oil tape triggered broad-based panic selling. The index swung from an intraday high of 171,945.83 to a low of 168,471.78; ready-market volume jumped to 628.67 million shares (Rs27.02 billion) from Wednesday's 477.67 million (Rs22.64 billion) as participation surged. Of 499 companies traded, only 58 advanced against 406 decliners; Pakistan Refinery (-4.24%), SSGC (-4.14%) and TPL (-3.4%) led sector laggards, while Cnergyico PK topped volume with 99.4 million shares. Investors are now bracing for the SBP's monetary policy announcement due Monday. Sources: Business Recorder, The Express Tribune.
five_things.sentiment: sharp risk-off, heaviest loss in weeks

five_things.html: Brent crude settled up $3.29 (3.4%) at $101.21/bbl, its highest close since May, while WTI climbed $3.02 (3.25%) to $96.05, after the US and Iran traded their biggest wave of tanker strikes yet near the Strait of Hormuz — a corridor that carried roughly a fifth of global oil supply before the seven-month-old conflict, now running well below pre-war transit levels. Goldman Sachs flagged the risk of Brent surging above $120 if the escalation persists. Sources: Business Recorder, CNBC.

five_things.chip: Wall Street Falls A Fourth Day
five_things.html: US equities fell for a fourth straight session Thursday: the S&P 500 slipped 0.58% to 7,591.70, the Dow dropped 0.60% (-316.56 pts) to 52,064.10 and the Nasdaq eased 0.65% to 26,081.72, as August PPI data (+0.4% m/m, +5.4% y/y) reaccelerated wholesale inflation and oil topped $100/bbl. The 10-year Treasury yield jumped nearly 10bps to 4.94%, its highest since October 2023, while the 2-year hovered near 4.38% as markets priced roughly a 71% chance the Fed delivers a 25bp hike at next week's 15-16 September FOMC meeting under Chair Kevin Warsh. Sources: CNBC, Tipp Insights.

Away from the war premium, Gulf non-oil economies kept expanding: the UAE's S&P Global PMI rose to 55.3 in August from 52.7 in July, its fastest growth since December 2024, while Saudi Arabia's Riyad Bank PMI climbed to 53.8, a six-month high, with output and new orders both accelerating. OPEC+'s seven core producers held October quotas unchanged at their 6 September virtual meeting, keeping the combined ceiling near 31.01m bpd as the group prioritises stability over added volume amid the Hormuz disruption. Sources: Arabian Business, ANI.

five_things.chip: Gold, Silver Ease Ahead Of Fed
five_things.html: Gold slipped to $4,383/oz (-0.3%) and silver eased to $66.62/oz (-1.0%) on Thursday as investors squared positions ahead of the PPI print and next week's FOMC decision, even as haven demand stayed underpinned by the unresolved Hormuz conflict; ETF inflows into gold have totalled roughly $18bn this year. Both metals remain firmly inside their 2026 uptrend. Sources: Yahoo Finance, USAGOLD.

matrix.local_html: The KSE-100 plunged 3,078.55 points (1.79%) to close at 168,865.04 on Thursday — its steepest single-day fall in weeks — as intensifying US-Iran tanker strikes near the Strait of Hormuz and a surging oil tape drove panic selling across the board, led by Pakistan Refinery, SSGC and TPL. Ready-market volume surged to 628.67 million shares (Rs27.02bn) from Wednesday's 477.67 million (Rs22.64bn), with only 58 of 499 traded names advancing. On policy, the government's Sovereign Wealth Fund (Amendment) Bill, 2026 remains before the Senate Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue, a governance overhaul the IMF is expected to scrutinise when its fourth EFF/third RSF review mission lands on 23 September. August CPI held elevated at 11.15% y/y, the SBP's policy rate stays at 11.5% ahead of Monday's rate announcement, 6-month KIBOR sits near 11.87%, and USD/PKR interbank was broadly steady at 277.35 versus Wednesday's 277.36. Sources: Business Recorder, Dawn.
matrix.gcc_html: Gulf oil benchmarks surged as the US-Iran conflict intensified around the Strait of Hormuz: Brent settled at $101.21/bbl (+3.4%), its highest close since May, and WTI climbed to $96.05, even as OPEC+'s seven core producers — Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman — held October quotas unchanged at their 6 September meeting, keeping the combined ceiling near 31.01m bpd and prioritising stability over volume. Away from the war premium, non-oil momentum held up well: the UAE's PMI hit 55.3 in August, its best since December 2024, with new business at a joint two-year high, and Saudi Arabia's PMI rose to a six-month high of 53.8 as output and new orders accelerated. Sources: Business Recorder, Gulf News.
matrix.global_html: US equities fell for a fourth consecutive session Thursday as August PPI data reaccelerated wholesale inflation (+0.4% m/m, +5.4% y/y) and oil topped $100/bbl, denting the outlook for margins and rate cuts: the S&P 500 slipped 0.58% to 7,591.70, the Dow dropped 0.60% to 52,064.10 and the Nasdaq eased 0.65% to 26,081.72. The 10-year Treasury yield jumped nearly 10bps to 4.94%, its highest since October 2023, and the 2-year held near 4.38%, with fed funds futures now pricing roughly a 71% chance of a 25bp hike at next week's 15-16 September FOMC meeting under Chair Kevin Warsh, who struck a hawkish tone at Jackson Hole. Congress has already passed a continuing resolution extending federal funding through 11 December, removing a near-term shutdown risk. Gold eased to $4,383/oz and silver to $66.62/oz as investors squared positions ahead of the Fed decision. Sources: CNBC, Federal News Network.

legislative.policy_html: Sovereign Wealth Fund (Amendment) Bill, 2026 — still before the Senate Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue, tightening SWF governance, fiscal safeguards and disclosure ahead of the IMF's fourth EFF/third RSF review mission due 23 September.
legislative.sectors: State-owned enterprises, sovereign fund-held assets, banks
legislative.impact_html: Wins: Investors and IMF stakeholders gain clearer governance and disclosure standards, supporting the case for the next EFF/RSF tranche. Loses: SWF-held state enterprises face tighter accountability and reporting obligations, raising near-term compliance costs.

legislative.policy_html: OPEC+'s seven core producers held October output quotas unchanged at their 6 September meeting, keeping the combined ceiling near 31.01m bpd as Brent trades above $100/bbl on Hormuz disruption.
legislative.sectors: Oil & gas majors, Gulf shipping/insurance, non-oil private sector
legislative.impact_html: Wins: Producers capturing higher realised prices without added supply, and Gulf non-oil sectors riding strong UAE and Saudi PMI momentum. Loses: Gulf shippers, insurers and energy importers exposed to a persistent Hormuz risk premium.

legislative.policy_html: The Fed's 15-16 September FOMC meeting under Chair Kevin Warsh is now a near-coin-flip on a 25bp hike (~71% odds per fed funds futures) after hot August PPI data and oil above $100/bbl; Congress has already passed a stopgap funding bill extending federal funding through 11 December.
legislative.impact_html: Wins: Rate-sensitive value and financials if the Fed signals a measured, data-dependent path. Loses: Growth and long-duration tech names if a hike is delivered into an oil-driven inflation shock, reinforcing the four-day equity slide.

desk_stance_html: Thursday's surge in volume (628.67m shares vs Wednesday's 477.67m) alongside the sharpest single-day loss in weeks points to genuine distribution rather than a technical wobble, as Brent above $101/bbl on an unresolved Hormuz tanker war and a hot PPI print reinforcing a near-coin-flip 15-16 September FOMC decision both remain unresolved risks. With the index holding just above the 168,000 psychological floor, we'd stay defensive on broad beta into next week's SBP rate decision and FOMC, while retaining selective exposure to E&P and refinery-adjacent names geared to a firmer oil tape and to non-oil GCC plays benefiting from resilient UAE and Saudi PMIs. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.

Good morning — here's the ContexAi Research desk's read on markets for Friday, 11 September 2026, covering Thursday's close.

THE OVERNIGHT TAPE
US equities fell for a fourth straight session: the S&P 500 slipped 0.58% to 7,591.70, the Dow dropped 0.60% (-316.56 pts) to 52,064.10 and the Nasdaq eased 0.65% to 26,081.72, as August PPI data (+0.4% m/m, +5.4% y/y) reaccelerated wholesale inflation and oil topped $100/bbl. Gold eased to $4,383/oz (-0.3%) and silver to $66.62/oz. Brent settled at $101.21/bbl (+3.4%), its highest close since May, and WTI climbed to $96.05.

PAKISTAN
The KSE-100 plunged 3,078.55 points (1.79%) to close at 168,865.04 on Thursday, its steepest single-day fall in weeks, as intensifying US-Iran tanker strikes near the Strait of Hormuz and a surging oil tape triggered panic selling led by Pakistan Refinery, SSGC and TPL. Ready-market volume surged to 628.67 million shares (Rs27.02bn) from Wednesday's 477.67 million, with only 58 of 499 traded names advancing. On policy, the government's Sovereign Wealth Fund (Amendment) Bill, 2026 remains before the Senate Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue ahead of the IMF's fourth EFF/third RSF review mission due 23 September. August CPI held elevated at 11.15% y/y, the SBP's policy rate stays at 11.5% ahead of Monday's rate announcement, 6-month KIBOR sits near 11.87%, and USD/PKR interbank was broadly steady at 277.35.

GCC
Gulf oil benchmarks surged as the US-Iran conflict intensified around the Strait of Hormuz, with Brent settling at $101.21/bbl, its highest close since May, even as OPEC+'s seven core producers held October quotas unchanged at their 6 September meeting, keeping the combined ceiling near 31.01m bpd. Non-oil momentum held up well despite the war premium: the UAE's PMI hit an August reading of 55.3, its best since December 2024, and Saudi Arabia's PMI rose to a six-month high of 53.8.

GLOBAL
US equities fell for a fourth consecutive session as hot PPI data and oil above $100/bbl weighed on sentiment, while Congress has already passed a stopgap funding bill extending federal funding through 11 December, removing near-term shutdown risk. Traders are pricing a near-coin-flip 15-16 September FOMC decision under Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, who struck a hawkish tone at Jackson Hole. Gold and silver eased as investors squared positions ahead of the Fed decision.

LEGISLATIVE TRACKER
• Pakistan: The Sovereign Wealth Fund (Amendment) Bill, 2026 remains before the Senate Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue, tightening governance ahead of the IMF's review mission due 23 September.
• GCC: OPEC+ held October quotas steady at its 6 September meeting, prioritising stability as Brent trades above $101/bbl.
• Global: The Fed's 15-16 September FOMC meeting is a near-coin-flip on a 25bp hike after hot PPI data, with a funding stopgap already passed through 11 December.

THE DAY AHEAD
KSE-100 — Support 168,472 (Thursday's intraday low; deeper support 167,000) · Pivot 168,865 (Thursday's close) · Resistance 171,946 (Thursday's intraday high, then Wednesday's close near 171,944).

Desk stance: Thursday's surge in volume alongside the sharpest single-day loss in weeks points to genuine distribution rather than a technical wobble, as Brent above $101/bbl on an unresolved Hormuz tanker war and a hot PPI print reinforcing a near-coin-flip FOMC decision both remain unresolved risks. With the index holding just above the 168,000 psychological floor, we'd stay defensive on broad beta into next week's SBP rate decision and FOMC, while retaining selective exposure to E&P and refinery-adjacent names geared to a firmer oil tape and to non-oil GCC plays benefiting from resilient UAE and Saudi PMIs.
